The grieving tiefling pair at the gate face off with Sazza. Arka is set on killing Sazza as indirect revenge for the death of Kanon, who was slain by goblins.

Arka and Memnos are idle in the druid grove after going to confront the captive goblin Sazza. The goblin may or may not have been killed in this prior scene. Arka remains bitter over the recent death of their friend, Kagha, while Memnos, if present, tries to shake her out of it.

Several conditions of conversations between Arka and Memnos here: Sazza escaped, sazza was killed, the pair wait for the goblin attack at the gates, or Arka's brother, Kanon, has been killed by goblins.

Kanon was manning the mechanism that opened the gate to the Druid Grove. He was trying to open the gate to let Aradin and the player through when he was killed by approaching goblins. Here, the player is using the Speak With Dead spell on his corpse. He is ashamed that he was not able to open the gate, and believes that he's killed Aradin and the rest because of that failure. That said, he still speaks like a corpse - serious, detached, a bit spooky.
context: Arka and Memnos are a grieving pair of tieflings at the grove gate after a recent goblin attack; Arka is kneeling over the corpse of Kanon (her brother), who was killed while trying to open the gate. Anguish and fury have driven Arka to train a crossbow on Sazza, a captive goblin she holds responsible for the deaths. Memnos, when present, tries to steady Arka or pull her back from violence. At the start of this scene the player can step between them and attempt to convince Arka not to shoot Sazza.
